links.note: Both print their engines whole: Agnikul’s Agnilet and Relativity’s Aeon are single-piece 3D-printed designs.
LeoLabs watches LEO from the ground with phased-array radar; Digantara is building the same picture from orbit.
GalaxEye goes further than ICEYE’s single sensor by fusing SAR with optical on one satellite.
Same name, different businesses - Canada’s Kepler Communications builds an optical relay network, India’s Kepler Aerospace does RF intelligence.
The green-propellant comparison: ECAPS’ LMP-103S has flown since 2010, Manastu’s hydrogen-peroxide blend is the Indian attempt at the same substitution for hydrazine.
Both replace street addresses with a short, speakable code so that deliveries and emergency services can find a doorstep.
Both put non-professionals in orbit - AMSAT through amateur radio clubs, Space Kidz through school and college teams.
Kleos chased the same RF-geolocation market and wound down in 2024; a reminder that the business model, not the physics, is the hard part.
The closest match on this page: a photonic gyroscope reduced to a chip, replacing spinning or fibre-optic inertial units.
Active debris removal as a commercial service - Astroscale has flown demonstrations, Cosmoserve is at design stage.
Both are aiming straight at full reusability, including the upper stage, rather than reusing the booster alone.
Manufacturing in orbit and bringing the product home - Varda returns pharmaceutical crystals, Inbound is building the lifting-body vehicle to do the same.
Space risk as a financial product rather than a technical one: broking and placing launch and in-orbit cover.
Both sell the view rather than the altitude: a slow pressurised capsule ride instead of a rocket.
Both are betting that compute in orbit beats downlinking the data - Starcloud on sunlight-powered data centres, TM2 on orbital data centres from India.
